tasks.short: Read research and assess emerging methods for finance analytics.

steps.what: Define research topics from current finance analytics problems.
Search research indexes and save relevant papers.
Read papers and record methods, findings, limitations and supporting passages.

loop.input: Accessible papers and a fixed research-note schema.
loop.output: Research notes with page references, quotations and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check references against source text; the scientist reads important passages and methods.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per paper; unreadable or unsupported content returns to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Methods and limitations appear in varied prose, equations and tables.

steps.what: Judge research quality and relevance to available finance data.
Write a short research brief with suggested experiments.

loop.input: Reviewed research notes, method shortlist and a brief template.
loop.output: Trend brief with attributed claims and proposed experiments.
loop.check: Each factual claim links to reviewed notes; the scientist checks recommendations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unresolved claims are omitted or marked for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: A useful synthesis connects findings across papers in plain language.

steps.what: Share the approved brief with finance analytics colleagues.

tasks.design: Configure alerts in research indexes under {OTHER} and deduplicate accessible papers into {DOCS}. A bounded extraction loop creates cited notes, and a drafting loop uses reviewed notes to prepare briefs. The scientist judges applicability and approves each brief before {WORKFLOW} distributes its link through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research alerts already existed. Reading varied papers and connecting findings to local finance problems still required substantial attention.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded text extraction can prepare traceable notes. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of connecting alerts, document templates and review queues.
tasks.still_hard: Technical validity, publication bias, inaccessible papers and transfer to local finance data still require careful reading.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an attractive result depends on assumptions that fail in the company's finance setting.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one finance analytics method for a small feasibility check.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to searching and first-pass notes; more goes to reproducing promising results. The scientist can recommend experiments more often, but gains no automatic spending or deployment authority.

reach.learn: Risk assumptions, validation standards and the cost of false alerts.

evidence.claim: Alerts, deduplication and document templates can handle collection and distribution; research appraisal remains judgement-heavy.
Cited extraction and drafting are plausible assistance, but the digest provides no documented research-reading case.
EU AI Act Article 4 requires AI literacy for relevant staff using AI systems.

assumptions: The scientist follows public research relevant to finance forecasting, risk or operations.
Research notes form most of the work; correspondence is a small share.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates.
The first version uses public papers and excludes confidential finance data from model inputs.
unknowns: Available research subscriptions and permitted automated access.
Approved model-processing arrangements and document retention rules.
Whether a weekly experiment shortlist would help the finance team.
research_questions: Can reviewers verify extracted limitations faster than writing notes themselves?
Which research sources provide reliable metadata and accessible full text?
new_work: Maintain research topics and source filters.
Handle inaccessible papers and extraction failures.
Refresh a small benchmark of papers with known findings.

tasks.short: Propose mathematical solutions to finance forecasting, allocation and risk problems.

steps.what: Agree the finance decision, constraints and success measures.
Extract finance data and reconcile it to agreed control totals.
Select mathematical methods and define assumptions and benchmarks.
Code models, run scenarios and compare results against benchmarks.
Interpret results and write a solution proposal with limitations.

loop.input: Validated results, approved assumptions, limitations and a proposal template.
loop.output: Draft solution proposal with links to calculated results.
loop.check: Numbers are inserted deterministically; the scientist checks interpretation, uncertainty and recommendations.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported explanations return to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining tradeoffs for a specific decision requires prose beyond fixed result tables.

steps.what: Review tradeoffs and approve a pilot or request changes.

tasks.design: A reusable project template in {WORKFLOW} connects an analysis brief to reconciled {ERP} data in {DATA_PLATFORM}. Versioned deterministic models generate scenarios, validation reports and {BI} views; a bounded loop drafts the proposal from verified results. The scientist approves its interpretation, and the finance manager separately approves the pilot.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance definitions, extraction code and validation routines differed between projects. Reusable components took time to build, while method choice remained specific to each problem.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can make reusable connectors, scenario runners and test harnesses cheaper to build. Established numerical methods still perform the calculations.
tasks.still_hard: Causal assumptions, leakage, changing business conditions and poorly specified objectives remain difficult. Creditworthiness uses involving natural persons can trigger EU AI Act high-risk requirements; GDPR applies when personal data is processed.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a defensible objective and explain why a mathematically strong result may be a poor finance decision.

ambition.what: A finance scenario clinic that compares cash, cost and service tradeoffs before pilot approval.

tasks.altitude: The scientist spends more of the week comparing assumptions and advising decision owners. Finance retains pilot and spending approval; any delegated experiment budget needs an explicit mandate.

reach.task: Compare budget scenarios under uncertain demand.
reach.learn: Budget ownership, forecast drivers and acceptable planning tolerances.

reach.task: Choose which analytics pilot deserves funding.
reach.learn: Investment hurdles, operational constraints and decision deadlines.

evidence.claim: Versioned numerical pipelines can calculate scenarios and validate results without a runtime model loop.
Copilot in Power BI supports report creation and semantic-model questions; this does not establish reliable mathematical method selection.
Uber documents faster query drafting alongside invented-table errors, supporting schema checks before execution.
EU AI Act Annex III includes specified creditworthiness uses involving natural persons.

assumptions: The initial scope covers recurring finance analysis patterns, not arbitrary new mathematical research.
Calculations use deterministic numerical code with reviewed specifications.
AI-assisted development is distinct from runtime automation.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one reusable analysis pattern.
unknowns: Available data interfaces and reconciliation controls.
How many past projects share a useful analysis pattern.
Whether proposed uses affect natural-person creditworthiness or other regulated decisions.
Personal data, permitted purposes and approved processing arrangements.
Who can approve pilots and experimental spending.
research_questions: Which repeated analysis pattern has stable definitions and a trustworthy baseline?
Can generated proposals preserve uncertainty without overstating recommendations?
new_work: Maintain reusable model templates and numerical tests.
Investigate reconciliation failures and unexpected scenario results.
Monitor deployed models for changing data and business conditions.

tasks.short: Choose survey populations and produce defensible samples or complete population lists.

steps.what: Agree survey objectives, population boundaries and required precision.
Assemble and reconcile the eligible population from source records.
Choose sampling or enumeration, strata and nonresponse assumptions.
Calculate sample sizes and allocations using statistical code.
Draw a reproducible sample or produce the complete eligible population list.
Approve coverage, selection integrity and the roster's release for survey preparation.

tasks.design: A deterministic pipeline in {DATA_PLATFORM} builds a permissioned population frame from the required {ERP} or {HCM} records and flags coverage gaps. The scientist specifies the design; tested formula code calculates allocation and produces a reproducible sample or complete roster with a selection log. A release control in {WORKFLOW} exposes the roster only after the scientist approves it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Population definitions and source identifiers varied between surveys. Frame cleaning and selection records were often rebuilt for each exercise.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable frame checks, explicit design forms and tested sampling code can now be assembled with less development effort. No model loop is needed once the scientist supplies the design.
tasks.still_hard: Missing populations, nonresponse bias and small subgroups can invalidate nominal precision. GDPR limits roster access and retention; employee surveys may require consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the population frame and response assumptions support the conclusion the finance team wants to draw.

ambition.what: Sampling support for smaller cost-centre teams previously omitted from finance planning surveys.

tasks.altitude: The scientist spends less time assembling lists and more time checking coverage and precision. Method and roster approval remain with the scientist; no new authority to contact people is assumed.

reach.task: Design a sample for a finance control test.
reach.learn: Audit objectives, tolerable error and why survey precision differs from audit assurance.

reach.task: Estimate cost drivers from a representative internal survey.
reach.learn: Cost-centre structure and how missing responses affect forecast assumptions.

evidence.claim: Explicit sampling designs, formula-based allocation and seeded selection can use deterministic code.
The PowerGPT evaluation separates model-assisted test selection from statistical-engine computation; its clinical results do not validate this survey workflow.
Population coverage and nonresponse assumptions require judgement despite automated sample selection.

assumptions: The example is an internal finance cost-driver survey; only necessary source records are used.
Population and design inputs are entered explicitly rather than inferred from prose.
Existing statistical code is reused where it has suitable checks.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates; consultation elapsed time can exceed working effort.
unknowns: Which records define the eligible population and who may access them.
Whether stable identifiers and subgroup attributes exist.
Required precision, response rates and acceptable disclosure thresholds.
Applicable national consultation rules and existing employee agreements.
Whether smaller teams can be included without exposing individual responses.
research_questions: How much undercoverage exists when the source frame is compared with an independent population count?
Which proposed subgroup estimates remain useful under realistic nonresponse?
new_work: Resolve missing or conflicting population records.
Maintain sampling formulas and reproducibility checks.
Review coverage, response assumptions and roster releases.
Remove expired rosters and audit access.

tasks.short: Design and test surveys that collect useful finance planning data.

steps.what: Agree the decisions, measures and respondent burden the survey must address.
Draft questions, response scales and routing in a document.

loop.input: Measurement brief, approved question library and instrument schema.
loop.output: Draft questionnaire with scales, routing and links to intended measures.
loop.check: Validate schema and routing; the scientist checks neutrality, construct coverage and unnecessary personal questions.
loop.stop: One draft and two revisions; unresolved measurement issues return to the scientist.
loop.why_not_simpler: New finance concepts need wording adapted to respondents; established items are reused directly.

steps.what: Review measurement quality, privacy, accessibility and respondent burden.
Build the survey form and test routing, validation and export fields.
Complete a supervised pilot and explain confusing questions.
Revise the instrument and document its measures and coding.
Approve the instrument for distribution after required reviews are complete.

tasks.design: A versioned question library in {DOCS} supplies established items, while a bounded loop drafts only the wording needed for new measures. Configured forms in {WORKFLOW} implement routing and validation, and deterministic generators produce the data dictionary and test report. The scientist reviews measurement quality and pilot feedback before a separate release approval; invitations remain a downstream action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Question wording, form configuration and coding documents were maintained separately. Automating form creation did little to solve unclear measures or misunderstood questions.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured instrument definitions can drive forms, tests and documentation together. A bounded drafting loop can suggest wording while keeping established questions and human pilot testing.
tasks.still_hard: Neutral wording, valid measures, translation and credible anonymity remain difficult. GDPR requires an appropriate basis, minimisation and retention controls; employee surveys may need consultation under national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Notice what respondents misunderstand or hesitate to disclose, and decide whether a question should be asked at all.

ambition.what: A short cost-driver pulse survey that supplements quarterly finance forecasts.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to form setup and duplicate documentation; more goes to pilot interviews and measurement quality. The scientist retains instrument design responsibility, while the finance manager retains release approval.

reach.task: Collect explanations for changing cost and demand assumptions.
reach.learn: Which respondent answers can support a forecast adjustment.

reach.task: Review employee survey collection and disclosure arrangements.
reach.learn: Purpose limits, retention, anonymity and applicable national consultation requirements.

evidence.claim: Configured forms can implement routing and validation; a shared instrument schema can generate coding documentation.
Question drafting can be assisted, but the digest provides no direct case establishing survey validity from generated wording.
Human pilot interviews help identify misunderstood concepts and response burden.
For the Netherlands, the digest identifies works-council consent requirements for specified individual staff-performance systems; applicability depends on the survey's use.

assumptions: The survey collects internal cost-driver information rather than individual performance ratings.
The existing form capability supports routing, access controls and structured export.
Pilot participation and review remain human activities.
Time shares include participant and approver effort, not only the scientist's time.
Build ranges cover one instrument family; consultation and pilot scheduling can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Available form features and approved question libraries.
Respondent groups, languages and accessibility needs.
Who approves measurement quality, privacy arrangements and release.
Whether responses can be anonymous and whether linkage is necessary.
research_questions: Do respondents interpret generated questions as the measurement brief intends?
Can one instrument definition reliably generate forms, routing tests and the data dictionary?
Does a short pulse survey improve forecast decisions enough to justify respondent effort?
new_work: Review new wording and maintain approved question versions.
Run pilot interviews and resolve ambiguous questions.
Maintain routing tests and export mappings.
Manage retention, access and release records.
Monitor respondent burden and survey fatigue.

role.altitude: The finance data scientist spends less time collecting papers, rebuilding extracts, drawing samples and maintaining duplicate documents. More time goes to framing decisions, validating assumptions and testing whether people can use the results; spending, release and regulated decision rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Help budget analysts connect survey measures and scenario results to forecast assumptions.
Help accountants and auditors distinguish sampling precision from audit assurance.
Help financial risk specialists assess method limitations and monitoring needs.
Help compliance officers review personal-data use and survey disclosure arrangements.
skills_to_grow: Reusable numerical pipelines and meaningful validation tests.
Sampling, measurement validity and nonresponse analysis.
Decision facilitation and clear explanation of uncertainty.
GDPR, relevant EU AI Act requirements and applicable national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a finance evidence service that combines research appraisal, representative data collection and reproducible scenario analysis before material planning decisions. Start with one recurring decision and measure whether better evidence changes its outcome.
